_about: Heavy fighter (design doc, Initial unit roster: air). EVERY VALUE IS A PLACEHOLDER proposed by Track S on 2026-10-09 so the demo can fly; the unit design sheet and its variant boards replace them. Plausible for a WWII twin-engine fighter (P-38, Bf 110, Beaufighter class) at true scale: about as fast as the light fighter, heavier and less agile. Record shape: data/units/_schema.json.
name: Heavy fighter

size_m._reason: twin-engine fighter span: P-38 15.8 m, Bf 110 16.3 m

draught_m._reason: a unit that does not float needs no water under it (the water rule, World.set_water, applies to domain sea only): 0

actions_per_turn._reason: Alex 2026-10-09 accepted this as the demo baseline. Was proposed: fast but less agile than the light fighter: one decision point fewer; 4 steps of 1.25 s in a 5 s turn

health._reason: between the light fighter and the bomber

sight_range_m._reason: Alex 2026-10-09 accepted the lead's fog recommendation (about 800 m so sight edges show at play zoom). Was proposed: same as the light fighter; unused until Track F's vision rule

material._reason: PROPOSED by builder G3 (2026-10-12; the board's table, variants/gunfire/board.json material_table, which Alex's decisions damage-looks, 'the model makes sense', and gunfire-looks, G3, put to use): an airframe is metal. Decides what a round that lands on it does (data/fx/fx.json gunfire): metal.

source_m._reason: one engine's smoke, not the 16 m span (the lead's 'about 8 m at most', decision impact-by-round-and-target: puffs are not sized by the unit's length): the same source as the light fighter's, so the trail is smaller than the old 0.34 to 0.8 of 16 m. ALEX (decision smoke-consistency, 2026-10-12), asked whether the heavy fighter's and the bomber's trails should stay at that new, smaller size: 'Yes to both'. So it stays 8 m (a board may still pick another)

source_back_m._reason: where the smoke leaves the plane: 5 m behind its centre, about the old 0.35 x 16 m (W1 tail_frac)

rise_mps._reason: ALEX (decision smoke-consistency, 2026-10-12), asked 'should planes' trails rise like ground smoke, and should the heavy fighter's and bomber's trails stay at their new, smaller size?': 'Yes to both'. So a plane's damage trail CLIMBS at 4 m/s, the same rate as a tank's, a boat's and the ruins' and wrecks' smolder (data/fx/fx.json ruin and crash smolder rise_mps), through the same model: a puff keeps the height it was born at, climbs and drifts with the wind at its height (fx_field.gd puff_drift), so an old puff of a low plane leans further downwind. It was 0 (PROPOSED by builder SMOKE, 2026-10-11: 'a puff climbing 4 m/s would lift an old puff by 100 m in its life'); Alex's answer ends that difference, and the fall trail of a plane out of control climbs with it (no jump at the moment it goes down). The number 4 is the ground smoke's, test_smoke_consistency holds the two equal

shape._about: One box. A plane's base is its BAND's absolute height. Every number PROPOSED.

stamp._reason: a target, not scenery: other lines are not blocked by it

length_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 12 m, a twin-engine fighter's length (P-38 11.5 m)

width_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 16 m, the unit's size_m (the wingspan)

bottom_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 1.2 m under the band's height

top_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 2 m over it: the tail fins and the gondola's top

speed_min_mps._reason: stall about 180 km/h, heavier wing loading than the light fighter

speed_cruise_mps._reason: about 380 km/h; long-range twins cruised a little faster

speed_max_mps._reason: about 595 km/h, P-38 class at low altitude

dive_speed_max_mps._reason: heavy aircraft gain speed fast in a dive

accel_mps2._reason: two engines but more mass: cruise to top in about 17 s (3-4 turns)

decel_mps2._reason: more momentum to shed than the light fighter

turn_rate_curve_dps._reason: three quarters of the light fighter's rate at each point: a 24 s circle at cruise

turn_bleed_mps2._reason: above its 3.5 m/s^2 of thrust, so a sustained hard turn costs speed

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: induced drag grows with the square of the load factor

bands_per_step._reason: one band per step keeps a climb a deliberate, visible choice

climb_speed_cost_mps._reason: more mass to lift than the light fighter

dive_speed_gain_mps._reason: heavier aircraft gain a little more in a dive; still less than the climb costs

round._reason: PROPOSED by builder G3 (decision round-model, 2026-10-12): the heavy fighter's cannon (2 pips a hit, 600 m) fires a small cannon round (the board's mapping, variants/gunfire/families.json rounds nose_cannon: small): not a machine gun's bullet (decision tracers-mg lists machine guns only), lighter than the tank's gun

hardpoints._reason: the lead's engagement-cones proposal (variants/engagement-cones/weapons_proposed.json), shown to Alex 2026-10-09, not yet decided. On the nose, 8 m forward of the centre

base_hit_chance._reason: Track C proposal (not in the lead's sheet): a cannon fires less often and hits harder: 2 pips at 0.3 once a second is 0.6 pips a second on a centred target, about the pair of machine guns, at a longer range and in a narrower cone

rim_odds_factor._reason: Track C proposal: a fixed gun is peaked (the lead's sheet: 'better near the centre'; Alex: a machine gun has better odds the closer the target is to the centre of its cone): a target on the rim has a fifth of the centre's odds

falloff_exponent._reason: Track C proposal: a quadratic fall (r squared) keeps the odds high through the inner half and drops them near the rim

tracking_dps._reason: Track C proposal (Alex 2026-10-10: relative velocity affects accuracy): the line-of-sight turn rate, degrees a second, at which crossing halves this gun's odds. A fixed gun is aimed by swinging the whole plane, so it tolerates little: the heavy fighter swings slower and the cannon is the narrower cone, so a little less than the light fighter's 8

rolls_per_second._reason: Track C proposal (not in the lead's sheet): a cannon is slower than machine guns: a roll a second
